A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Landscape of Thoughts work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original reasoning-landscape analyses, model and decoding-method evaluations, verifier accuracy experiments, and supplementary tokenization and process-verifier experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds consistency analyses, MMLU-Pro evaluation, verifier-feature ablations and dimensionality-reduction comparisons.

M1.justification: The perplexity-based state features, default t-SNE visualization, three metrics, random-forest verifier and weighted voting remain. The process-verifier variant already appears in v2. New ablations and prospective extensions do not establish a changed proposed algorithm; omission of the smoothing specification is a documentation loss.

E1.justification: V3 adds the harder, reasoning-focused MMLU-Pro Math evaluation in Appendix D.3. AQuA, MMLU, StrategyQA and CommonsenseQA remain. QwQ and DeepSeek reasoning-model examples were already evaluated in v2's appendix, so their later prominence does not establish new task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 Figure 13 adds evaluated UMAP and PaCMAP alternatives alongside t-SNE. The separate LtM/L2M comparison on StrategyQA in v2 Figure 10 disappears from the corresponding landscape comparison. Voting and outcome/process-verifier comparators remain; the added discussion of external and model-self verifiers does not report empirical comparisons against them.

E3.justification: New controlled designs include randomly assembled chains of 2–32 thoughts, rescoring identical 70B-generated CoTs with four models, and verifier-feature ablations across sampling budgets. These substantially expand the evaluation design. The existing setup of 20 training questions, 50 test questions and ordinarily 10 sampled trajectories remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds analyses of trajectories that approach correct answers before failing, consistency versus length and random thoughts, task difficulty, shared-CoT perplexity, verifier-feature contributions and projection robustness. These test several previously unexamined explanations and confounds. Existing sentence-tokenization and process-verifier analyses are retained, while the separate LtM-on-StrategyQA landscape analysis is removed.

E5.justification: Appendix D.3 adds an explicitly identified Pearson-correlation estimate for thought count versus consistency, reporting -0.0185. Existing Appendix D.1 p-values and plotted error bars remain unchanged. V3 adds no seed information, repeated-experiment counts, confidence intervals or explanation of the existing error bars.

E6.justification: Substantial new findings concern failure trajectories, consistency controls, MMLU-Pro, shared-CoT perplexity and feature ablations. For example, Table 9 reports 3B StrategyQA accuracy of 0.66 with combined features versus 0.32 and 0.30 with individual features at 50 paths. Matched headline plots and v2 Tables 1–3, now Tables 1, 6 and 7, retain their values. New MMLU entries are additional results, not established same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: V2's explicit Parzen-window definition of smoothed landscape density, Equation 2.5, is removed without an equivalent formula elsewhere in v3. Other state and anchor definitions, metrics, voting and statistical-verification formulas remain mathematically equivalent. The expanded perplexity factorization is explanatory; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the novelty wording from the first visualization tool to the first landscape visualization tool. The central contributions—reasoning visualization, behavioral observations and a lightweight verifier improving accuracy and test-time scaling—remain substantively intact.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands interpretations of the relationship between landscapes and metrics, feature complementarity and projection robustness. Appendices A.5–A.7 discuss pruning, post-hoc reasoning detection, distractor quality and code-generation extensions while retaining the multiple-choice limitation. These are prospective capabilities, not validated extensions. V2's impact statement, including its alignment-bypass misuse concern, is removed.

D1.justification: V3 documents the random-thought experiment's temperature of 0.7, question and chain counts, recombination procedure, and shared-CoT generation/rescoring setup. Conversely, it drops the smoothing kernel and bandwidth explanation from v2. Existing verifier training/test sample disclosures and the public code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds positioning against uncertainty, consistency and hallucination-detection approaches, with citations including Li, Chuang and Xiong, plus literature supporting projection alternatives and MMLU-Pro. The Mixtral and Silverman references disappear. Most earlier research positioning remains; moving related work into Appendix B is separately a structural change.

P1.justification: The introduction and method exposition are extensively revised, terminology shifts toward LoT and trajectories, and textual states are distinguished more clearly from numerical features. Model comparisons move ahead of method comparisons, related work moves to Appendix B, and limitations move from the conclusion into an expanded appendix. The appendix organization changes substantially.

P2.justification: V3 changes the document template, margins, typography, headers, affiliation logos and figure sizing. It adds diagnostic tables and the projection-comparison figure, moves QwQ visualization into the main text, and redisplays the revised 8B case study there. The LtM StrategyQA figure is removed. Most original plots are retained despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new projection, shared-CoT perplexity and verifier-feature controls address validation gaps in v2, while clearer explanations improve interpretability. Benefits are tempered by lost smoothing documentation and overstatement in some new interpretations: Table 3's values do not consistently decrease with chain length as claimed. The additions provide a useful but limited net quality improvement.
